seo_title: Cost of Living in Seoul 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Seoul per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of South Korea: visa-free for Russians for up to 60 days (a K-ETA authorisation is required), ultra-fast internet, safety and convenient transport. Downsides are high rents, the language barrier and the intense pace.
pros: Visa-free for up to 60 days (a K-ETA authorisation is required)
cons: A very intense pace and high density
Cold winters and hot, humid summers

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Seoul?
faq.answer: No, visa-free for up to 60 days, but you need to arrange a K-ETA online authorisation in advance.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Seoul?
faq.answer: Expensive, especially rent; but the service and transport are world-class. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Seoul?
faq.answer: Korean; there's little English in daily life, so translation apps come in handy.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Seoul?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need a card from a foreign bank or local payment apps.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Seoul?
faq.answer: Temperate monsoon: cold, dry winters and hot, humid summers with rain.

faq.question: What is K-ETA?
faq.answer: An electronic travel authorisation arranged online before the trip under the visa-free regime.

reviews.text: Seoul means internet, transport and safety at their best — the city never sleeps. The downsides are expensive rent and the language barrier; Korean is almost a must.
I fell in love with the service and the culture, everything works perfectly. Living is expensive and intense, and it's tricky in places without Korean, but it's incredibly high-tech.
